summary: SSE stream stalls mid-response when client sends very large system message with chunked transfer encoding
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that SSE (server-sent events) chat sessions stall partway through generation when their client sends a large system message using HTTP chunked transfer-encoding. The stream initially returns tokens for ~2-6s, then goes silent and eventually the client observes a timeout. This affects a subset of long-context chats when the initial system payload exceeds ~256KB and is uploaded as chunked data by their SDK/proxy.

Impact:
- Multiple customer production chats stall mid-generation causing degraded UX for live assistants.
- Observed only on the customer's Dedicated pool in us-east; no widespread host-level outage.
- Severity: blocks live sessions for affected customers (Sev1 / P1).

Environment:
- Dedicated customer pool (reserved) in us-east.
- API endpoint: hosted redwood inference (https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream).
- Customer uses an intermediate API proxy that streams a large system prompt via chunked transfer-encoding.
- Affected model(s): redwood-v2-1b and redwood-v2-3b.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Client opens SSE chat request to /v1/chat/stream with headers: Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Content-Type: application/json.
2) Large system message (~300KB) is sent in several chunks; client then sends the user prompt.
3) Server starts streaming tokens normally for 2-6 seconds (first chunk of output arrives).
4) Streaming output pauses; no further SSE events for the duration of the generation window.
5) Eventually client-side timeout or user cancels session.

Observed logs/traces/snippets:
- API gateway logs (request_id=rs-0a9f4b2c) show request accepted and worker assigned (worker=ded-12).
- Worker logs show token emission up to token 48, then no further token writes. No explicit worker crash.
- Edge proxy logs show an HTTP/1.1 chunked body sequence where the final chunk (0\r\n) is not received for ~4s after streaming started.
- Serving runtime trace indicates thread blocking at request-body-read step while generator coroutine awaits further input, leading to worker entering a "waiting on request body" state.
- No 5xx returned; connection remains established until client-side timeout.

Hypothesis:
- Our runtime begins token generation as soon as it has parsed the prompt structure, but in this code path we still synchronously attempt to drain the entire request body (to confirm JSON integrity) before allowing the generator to proceed to completion. When the client uploads the system message via chunked encoding and the last-chunk arrives late (due to upstream buffering or TCP coalescing), the runtime ends up blocking on request-body completion while the generator coroutine is producing tokens to the SSE writer. The combination leads to a deadlock where token emission is paused while the request-body reader waits for completion, producing the observed mid-stream silence.

Workarounds (customer-facing):
- Ask the customer to send the full JSON payload as a single request (avoid chunked transfer-encoding) or ensure the client flushes the final chunk before opening the SSE stream.
- If immediate fix needed, use non-streaming calls (stream: false) as a temporary workaround so the full request body is processed synchronously before generation.

Investigation notes (engineering):
- Reproduced locally by using curl with --no-buffer and --upload-file split into chunks; local dedicated simulation reproduced the mid-stream pause.
- Trace correlation showed worker thread blocked in http-request parser (waiting for final chunk), while generator coroutine attempted to push more tokens but was gated by a request-body lock.
- Edge proxy (customer-managed) behavior influences timing — customers using aggressive TCP buffering or proxies that delay final chunk complete are more likely to hit this.
- Related to how the API gateway forwards chunked bodies to the dedicated worker: we forward as streaming body and currently rely on final chunk arrival to flip an internal "body complete" flag before certain cleanup/emit paths.

Next steps / action items:
- ENG: Implement non-blocking request-body drain so generation can continue while remaining bytes arrive. Create small canary that flips off the final-chunk dependency for SSE writers. (Assigned to Liam O'Connor, ETA: 2026-03-12).
- ENG: Add robust instrumentation around request-body read latencies to detect long-tail chunking patterns and alert if >500ms between chunks for long bodies. (Owner: Priya Malik).
- Support/SE: Provide customer-side guidance to ensure final chunk flush or to disable chunked uploads. (Owner: Asha Patel).

Comments:
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Asha Patel: Customer reported multiple live sessions stalling mid-generation; provided request_id rs-0a9f4b2c and a packet capture from their proxy. They can repro reliably when their SDK streams the system prompt in chunks.

2026-03-10 11:03 - Liam O'Connor: I reproduced locally using a chunked upload script against a dedicated dev pool and I see the exact pause behavior. Attaching trace: worker ded-12 deadlock-ish state where request-body read is blocking generator completion.

2026-03-10 14:47 - Priya Malik: Confirmed it's not kernel-level OOM or preemption; worker stays up. The trace indicates a lock inversion between body-reader and sse-writer. Planning a small runtime change to decouple body completion from streaming writes.
2026-03-11 08:22 - Asha Patel: Customer validated workaround by switching to a single non-chunked upload; streams proceed normally. They are okay with a temporary mitigation but want a permanent fix.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Liam O'Connor: PR created to perform body drain on a separate reader thread and to allow SSE writer to continue once JSON root object is parsed. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4912. Deploying to canary now.
2026-03-12 17:30 - Priya Malik: Canary observed for 6 hours with sample of chunked test vectors; no mid-stream stalls seen. Preparing staged rollout.
2026-03-12 18:05 - Asha Patel: Informed customer of pending production rollout; requested they run their test on staging to confirm.
investigation: Reproducer steps: used a Python script that writes JSON with a large 'system' key in 8KB chunks over an open HTTP/1.1 connection while polling the SSE endpoint. Observed ~3-5s silence window following initial tokens when the final chunk delayed. Heap/profile snapshots show no GC or CPU spike. Thread dump reveals 'http_body_reader' blocked on socket.read; generator coroutine awaiting request-body-lock. This is reproducible with controlled inter-chunk delays >250ms.
resolution: Engineering change merged (runtime PR #4912) to decouple SSE emission from final-chunk gating: parser now emits tokens after JSON root parse and drains remaining body asynchronously. Canary rollout (us-east dedicated canary) completed 2026-03-12 16:40 with no regressions. Staged global rollout scheduled 2026-03-13. Customer notified of fix and asked to validate on their end.
resolution_notes:
- Deployed fix to canary and validated with customer's chunked test vectors.
- Added metric 'request.body.interchunk_latency' and alert threshold for >500ms.
- Updated support KB with guidance on chunked uploads and recommended client behavior.
- Follow-up: Audit dedicated pool request-body handling to ensure consistency across all endpoints (task opened: INT-3350).
public_facing_summary: We identified and fixed an interaction where certain chunked request uploads could cause SSE chat streams to pause mid-generation. A runtime change was deployed to let streaming emission proceed while remaining request bytes arrive asynchronously; customers using chunked uploads should see normal behavior after the staged rollout.
